newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH PAPER INDUSTRY SAYS UNION DEAL POSSIBLE.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH PAPER INDUSTRY SAYS UNION DEAL POSSIBLE.

text.p: Resumed talks with the Paper Workers' Union have no special agenda, timetable or target, but agreement on some old unsolved issues is possible, the forest industry's chief negotiator Mauri Moren said on Wednesday.
He was due to meet the union's chairman Jarmo Lahteenmaki on Wednesday amid media reports that this marks a new start for talks on unresolved problems in for instance job delineation.
"I think talking should solve these things," Moren told Reuters.
But he declined to list the issues to be discussed, and referred to statements from the paper workers.

The union -- according to many experts a crucial party in attempts at a comprehensive national incomes deal with moderate pay hikes -- has said it cannot join a broad agreement due to the unsolved problems in the sector.
It has said one key issue is restricting the use of non-paper workers for maintenance jobs, although the supreme administrative court has already ruled in favour of the industry in the issue.
"I would not call this a disagreement, the court has ruled, and we are happy with that," Moren said.
He declined to give the forest industry's targets for the coming incomes settlement talks, but repeated that it would support a wide deal with moderate wage hikes.
